step:asking-an-imam.title: Ask an imam a good question
keyPoints: Says marriage, divorce, inheritance, zakat, abuse, medical and legal matters all need careful review, with professional help for medical, legal or financial issues.
Says online answers often differ because they follow different schools or someone else's situation, so note the source and school of each.
Recommends SeekersGuidance, New Muslim Academy and ICNA New Muslim Support (a US-based organisation) as resource cards.

step:character.title: Work on your character (akhlaq)
keyPoints: Quotes 'I was sent to perfect good character', 'best of you have the best character', 'actions are by intentions', the strong-man and 'best to their families' hadith; only generic sunnah-com id.
Cites Muslim 2749 (if people did not sin, Allah would bring people who sin and seek forgiveness), Muslim 2750a (Hanzala feared hypocrisy) and Quran 33:21.
Calls Martin Lings' 'Muhammad: His Life Based on the Earliest Sources' the usual first seerah; confirm it suits (Lings was a Perennialist Sufi). Resource card is Yasir Qadhi's Seerah.
Says nightly self-review (muhasabah) was a companions' practice, and advises 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' for everyday impatience such as traffic and queues.
preCheckFlags: Virtue list leads with Arabic: 'Sabr (patience)', 'Sidq (truthfulness)', 'Tawadu (humility)', 'Ihsan', 'Shukr', 'Rahmah'; the naming rule puts plain English first.

step:community.title: Find your local Muslim community
keyPoints: Names Convert Care at Islam Care Centre (Ottawa) and Convert Connect at MAC Masjid Toronto as convert programmes; confirm both still run and details are current.
Recommends Khalil Center, a Muslim mental health service (online only per its source note; clinicians' provincial registration not listed); confirm suitability.
Suggests joining a local WhatsApp or Telegram group for Muslims in your area; the step itself adds no privacy or safety caveat.
Recommends ICNA New Muslim Support (US-based), WhyIslam and AboutIslam's new-Muslim pages.
preCheckFlags: The JSON has two 'relatedLinks' keys; the second replaces the first, so 'Religion or custom? Examples' and 'Everyday phrases and how to reply' never show.

step:daily-dua-dhikr.title: Daily remembrance habit (dua and dhikr)
keyPoints: Says you can make dua in your own language, with no note that the Hanafi school restricts non-Arabic dua inside the prayer (the dua tool limits it to outside fixed recitation).
Recommends Fortress of the Muslim (Darussalam) as a sourced dua collection, plus Quran.com and New Muslim Academy.

step:family-and-friends.title: Tell your family and friends
keyPoints: Script for a Christian relative: 'Muslims believe he is the Messiah and a great prophet, and we honour Mary... God is one and has no son' (Quran 29:46 cited).
Says Islam holds you to good character and to keeping family ties, not cutting them.
Safety note: if telling someone could cost you housing or risk harm or control, speak to a local support person first; no named service or contact is given.
Online script: you do not owe anyone your story; wait until settled before posting about your Shahada (links the red flags guide).

step:fasting.title: Learn how fasting works (sawm)
keyPoints: Says 'in the Hanafi school' kissing or touching that leads to ejaculation breaks the fast; the other schools hold the same, so the attribution may mislead.
Exemptions: travel, illness, pregnancy or nursing at risk, menstruation (made up), fidyah only if never able; Diabetes Canada: see a doctor 1 to 3 months before Ramadan.
Says eating or drinking by forgetting does not break the fast (the Prophet called it a provision from Allah), and a Toronto winter fast is roughly ten hours.
Quotes Quran 2:183 but the specific id is 2:184; forgetful-eating and dates-and-water hadith have no ids; Nasa'i 2420 and Muslim 1164 are cited but not used in the text.
preCheckFlags: Validity line says a fast counts only if 'you are not in an exempt category' and omits intercourse; earlier the step lets travellers fast and lists intercourse as breaking it.

step:first-24-hours.title: Your first day as a Muslim
keyPoints: Says a Shahada certificate can help later for marriage, Hajj, Umrah or community records, but your Islam does not depend on paperwork.
Advises a safety plan before telling family if safety at home is a concern, and a trusted mentor first if hostility is expected; links red flags guide and Get help.
Says to start with faith, purification, the basics of prayer and someone to ask, and to ask a mentor for help with Ghusl.
Recommends New Muslim Academy, WhyIslam and Mustafa Umar's 'Welcome to Islam'.

step:first-jumuah.title: Go to your first Friday prayer
keyPoints: Says Friday prayer is an obligation for adult men and not required of women (Abu Dawud 1067); if a woman attends, it takes the place of Dhuhr.
Reports a Hanafi answer (Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam) that a job regularly preventing Jumuah attendance is not permitted, and tells readers to ask a scholar.
Says the Friday ghusl is recommended, not a condition, and wudu alone is valid (Abu Dawud 354); say Ameen with the imam after Al-Fatihah (Bukhari 780).
Says scholars differ on praying two rak'ahs when arriving during the sermon (Muslim 875c); do not step over people (Abu Dawud 1118).

step:first-masjid-visit.title: Visit a masjid for the first time
keyPoints: Says Convert Care at Islam Care Centre (Ottawa) and Convert Connect at MAC Masjid Toronto can arrange a guide for a first visit; confirm both are current.
Dress advice: men wear long pants and a sleeved shirt; women bring a scarf to enter the prayer area; many masjids keep spare scarves.
Etiquette: do not walk in front of someone praying (Bukhari 510); people repeat the adhan softly (Muslim 384); men and women usually pray separately.
Recommends ICNA New Muslim Support (US-based), WhyIslam and New Muslim Guide, and points to the in-app Masjid Finder.

step:ghusl.title: Make the full-body wash (ghusl)
keyPoints: Says ghusl is 'recommended' after Shahada; does not say it is required if you were in a state needing ghusl, or that Maliki/Hanbali require it (the wudu-ghusl tool does).
Says the minimum is water over the whole body plus intention; the Hanafi school also requires rinsing the mouth and nose and does not make intention a condition.
Its wudu sub-steps (face, arms, head, feet) leave out rinsing the mouth and nose, which the prayer step and the wudu tool include.
Says tayammum takes the place of ghusl when water is unavailable or unusable; only generic sources (New Muslim Guide, SeekersGuidance) are cited.

step:halal-eating-practical.title: Eat halal day to day
keyPoints: Recommends seafood as an easy early option, twice, with no note that the Hanafi school allows fish only (the halal-haram step says other seafood differs).
Says buy halal-certified meat when you can and look for certifiers you recognise locally; gelatin, enzymes, cross-contamination and standards vary.

step:halal-haram.title: Learn the halal and haram basics
keyPoints: Says the Hanafi school allows tiny non-wine alcohol in flavourings (e.g. vanilla extract) when it cannot intoxicate; cooking wine is out; alcohol-free is the careful choice.
Says many scholars and Canadian certifiers accept only zabiha, while others accept People of the Book meat under Quran 5:5 (AMJA fatwa cited).
Says fish is halal in every school and other seafood differs; everything is halal unless prohibited; leave doubtful matters; eating haram unknowingly carries no sin.
Says a Canadian halal label must name its certifier (CFIA), and names HMA and ISNA Canada Halal as common certifiers whose standards differ.

step:knowledge.title: Keep learning
keyPoints: Recommends Tariq Ramadan's 'In the Footsteps of the Prophet'; a Geneva appeals court convicted Ramadan of rape in 2024. Confirm the team still wants it listed.
Recommends AlMaghrib, Yaqeen, SeekersGuidance, Bayyinah (Nouman Ali Khan), and books by Asad Tarsin, Safiur Rahman Mubarakpuri and Hamza Yusuf.
Quotes 'Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim' (Ibn Majah 224, grading disputed), 'Whoever travels a path...' (Muslim 2699) and 'The cure for ignorance is to ask'.
Those hadith and 'the first word revealed was Iqra' have no specific ids; the only hadith-collection id is Ibn Sirin's saying in Muslim's introduction.

step:modesty-and-clothing.title: Take modesty one step at a time
keyPoints: States the minimum: men cover navel to knee; women cover all but face and hands in front of men who are not close relatives, all day (SeekersGuidance, Quran 24:30-31).
Scholar to confirm the 'all but face and hands' wording against school differences, e.g. Hanafi on the feet and the Hanbali view on the face.
If a visible change could provoke hostility or danger at home, talk to a local mentor or get support first; no named service is given.
Workplace dress rules: find out what is religiously required first, then make a specific accommodation request with local advice.

step:prayer-on-ramp.title: Ease into prayer without shame
keyPoints: Says Hanafis count holding and reading a Quran in prayer 'strongly disliked'; al-Hidayah reports Abu Hanifa held it invalidates the prayer. Says Shafi'is let a learner read Al-Fatihah.
Rung plan has beginners pray all five prayers in 'simple form', saying remembrance phrases before they know Al-Fatihah and before learning the tashahhud (rung 3).
For missed prayers, tells readers to ask a teacher how to make them up; recommends the Pillars app, New Muslim Guide and an Islamwise rak'ah video.

step:prayer.title: Start praying five times a day
keyPoints: Wudu: once is the minimum, three times Sunnah, head wiped once (the Shafi'i school makes three wipes Sunnah); broken by toilet, gas or deep sleep; bleeding differs.
If you lose count, take the lower number and add sujud al-sahw (the Hanafi rule differs for a first-time doubt); rak'ah counts 2, 4, 4, 3, 4.
Transliterations 'Subhana Rabbiyal Adheem', 'Subhana Rabbiyal A'la', 'As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah'; says the qibla from most of Canada is roughly northeast.
Says 'You have the right to pray' at work or school, and that schools differ on combining prayers for work (AMJA; SeekersGuidance Hanafi answer).

step:questions-and-doubts.title: Handle questions and doubts well
keyPoints: Cites Hanzala fearing he was a hypocrite when his feeling of faith faded at home, and the Prophet reassuring him (Sahih Muslim 2750a).
Says feeling unsettled or having doubts does not make you a bad Muslim, and to keep praying while waiting for answers.
Advises stepping away from content that leaves you anxious or hopeless; gives no mental health referral in the step itself (Get help is linked).
Recommends Yaqeen Institute, SeekersGuidance and New Muslim Academy for questions.

step:quran.title: Start reading the Quran
keyPoints: Recommends The Clear Quran (Mustafa Khattab), The Gracious Quran (Ahmad Zaki Hammad), Quran.com, an unnamed 'Al-Quran app' and the Tarteel AI app.
Recommends reciters Mishary Rashid Alafasy, Abdul Rahman Al-Sudais and Omar Hisham Al-Arabi.
Facts to confirm: revealed over 23 years; Al-Ikhlas has four verses; Al-Kawthar is the shortest surah (three verses); 114 chapters; Juz Amma is the 30th part.
Says reading a translation on its own is 'completely valid' while the Arabic is out of reach (for understanding, not for recitation in prayer).

step:shahada.title: Declare your faith (Shahada)
keyPoints: Transliteration 'Ash-hadu an la ilaha ill-Allah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasul-Allah' and its English meaning; no Arabic script is shown.
Says the Shahada wipes away what came before and counts said alone; 'Islam wipes out what came before' (Muslim 121) is not among this step's sources.
Tiny version lets someone say it in their own words ('I believe there is only one God and Muhammad is His messenger') with the Arabic later; confirm this counts.
Reports SeekersGuidance answers: Shireen Ahmed (better before others, not required), Abdurragmaan Khan (online Shahada valid), Yama Niazi ('ashhadu' more cautious).

step:zakat-hajj.title: Charity (zakat) and the pilgrimage (Hajj)
keyPoints: Zakat: 2.5% of qualifying wealth above nisab held a lunar year; nisab 87.48 g gold or 612.36 g silver (Islamic Relief Canada); home, car and belongings excluded.
Says subtract debts due now, with long-term debts treated differently; names NZF Canada and Muslim Welfare Canada calculators; check charities on the CRA list.
Travel advice is dated: 'checked September 23, 2026, page last updated September 17, 2026, avoid non-essential travel'; the source note says updated September 24.
Hajj: once if physically and financially able; says it 'lasts five to six days' and 'ends with Eid al-Adha' (Eid is 10 Dhul Hijjah; rites run to the 12th or 13th).
preCheckFlags: Heading 'Understand Sadaqah (voluntary charity)' puts the Arabic term first; the naming rule wants plain English first, e.g. 'Understand voluntary charity (sadaqah)'.

stage:day-0-1.title: Faith and a fresh start (Day 0-1)
keyPoints: Says changing your name is not required (scholars usually add: unless the name's meaning conflicts with Islam).
Says make Ghusl 'when you feel ready'; the wudu-ghusl tool says it is required before prayer if you were in a state needing ghusl.
Recommends Mustafa Umar's 'Welcome to Islam', described as a free 32-page guide on his website; confirm page count and free access.
Ask-for-help triggers include not feeling safe telling family and needing a witness or certificate; no contacts are named.

stage:week-1.title: Getting the basics in place (Week 1)
keyPoints: Says missing prayers while still learning is normal, and optional practices can wait until the required ones feel steady.
Recommends Quran.com's free 'Seven Days, Seven Verses' Al-Fatihah plan, readable without an account.
Recommends the New Muslim Academy prayer course and says it needs an account and the site uses analytics and an advertising pixel; confirm still true.

stage:week-2-3.title: Settling into practice (Weeks 2-4)
keyPoints: Recommends a masjid Arabic-reading class (letters, vowels, joining, short surahs) with The Clear Quran or Abdel Haleem's translation.
Recommends New Muslim Academy live Quran classes: free, evenings Eastern time, brothers and sisters taught separately, sign-up form first.
Ask-for-help triggers include family pressure turning unsafe or controlling and doubts that stop you functioning; no contacts are named.
Guardrails: free before paid, and be careful with one-to-one tutoring from academies you cannot check.

stage:month-1-2.title: Islam in daily life (Months 2-3)
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Academy core courses or SeekersGuidance's free live 'Essentials of Faith, Worship, and Spirituality', Saturdays 10:00 Eastern; confirm the schedule.
Recommends Quran.com learning plans for short surahs such as Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas.
Ask-for-help triggers: food or clothing pressure risking safety at home, a medical condition affecting fasting, a ruling on work, school or money.
Guardrail: choose a prayer times app that keeps your location on your phone and has no ads.

stage:month-3-6.title: Character and steady learning (Months 4-6)
keyPoints: Recommends Yaqeen Institute's free ebook 'Qur'an 30 for 30: Thematic Tafsir' by Dr. Omar Suleiman and Sh. Ismail Kamdar.
Recommends a local halaqa; guardrails say learn from a teacher you can meet or check, and skip debate channels in the first months.

stage:month-6-plus.title: Growth over a lifetime (Beyond 6 months)
keyPoints: Says Hajj is not owed until you are able to go, and zakat does not apply below the threshold (nisab).
Recommends MAC eLearning, free online courses from the Muslim Association of Canada.
Recommends Tafsir Ibn Kathir abridged (30th part), a paid Darussalam print book.

tool:dua-dhikr.title: Supplication and remembrance (dua and dhikr)
keyPoints: Anxiety section says dua is no substitute for help in crisis, self-harm or abuse; the anxiety dua (Bukhari 6369) cites 988-canada but no numbers appear on the page.
Adhan wording per Abu Dawud 499 (Hasan Sahih); iqama described as 'most phrases said once' (the Hanafi iqama doubles them); reply 'La hawla...' at the hayya lines (Muslim 385).
Hadith duas: after the adhan (Bukhari 614, Muslim 384), after salam (Muslim 591), sayyid al-istighfar (transliteration cut off with '...'; check the Arabic against Bukhari 6306).
Quranic duas 3:8, 2:201, 2:250, 23:109 and 20:25-28 (Musa's dua): check the Arabic, transliteration and translation of meaning.
Everyday phrases and gradings: Tirmidhi 2035 (hasan), Tirmidhi 3443 (hasan), Abu Dawud 2130 (sahih), Bukhari 6224, 1284, 3616; Eid greeting sourced to IslamQA 36442.
Other-words list: Namaz (Persian, Urdu, Turkish, Bengali), Roza (given as Persian and Urdu; Bengali also says roja), Abbu/abi, Ammi, Akhi, Ukhti, Habibi, Bhai.
preCheckFlags: Anxiety section intro mentions 'thinking of hurting yourself' but neither it nor the page's crisis box gives 911 first, then 9-8-8 (call or text), as CLAUDE.md requires.
Card heading 'Sayyid al-istighfar' leads with Arabic; the naming rule wants plain English first, e.g. 'The best way to ask forgiveness (sayyid al-istighfar)'.

tool:quran-starter.title: Quran starter path
keyPoints: Letter mistakes: Shafi'i says repeat the word, and the prayer is invalid only if the mistake changes meaning and is deliberate; Hanafi (Ibn Abidin): accidental saad/seen is fine.
Al-Fatihah word by word: Arabic, transliteration and meanings (e.g. 'Maliki' = 'Master', 'al-maghdubi' = 'those who earned anger'); check against the Quranic Arabic Corpus.
Sounds guide: ayn, heavy h, kha, ghayn 'close to a French r', qaf, the heavy letters, th/dh and shaddah; a tajweed teacher should confirm the tips.
Cites Bukhari 6464 (regular deeds), Muslim 798a (double reward for one who struggles to recite) and Quran 73:4; says you do not pause prayer until recitation is perfect.
Recommends Quran.com, The Clear Quran, New Muslim Academy classes, Mishary al-Afasy, Islamwise, Madinah Arabic (author unnamed, sells lessons) and Arabic 101 (sells classes).
Reading paths and week plan: Quran 39:53, 2:186, 23:109, Surah Yusuf, 20:14, 2:153 and Al-'Asr; learning timeline from week 1 to month 12 (basic tajweed).

tool:salah-companion.title: Learn to pray (salah)
keyPoints: Sequence and rak'ah map: Al-Fatihah plus a surah in rak'ahs 1-2 only, 'Rabbighfir li' between prostrations, first sitting after rak'ah 2, salawat only in the final sitting.
Arabic, transliteration and meaning for 11 recitations: takbir, Al-Fatihah, Al-Ikhlas, Al-'Asr, ruku and sujud phrases, Ibn Mas'ud's tashahhud, salawat Ibrahimiyyah, salam.
Before you can recite: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu akbar, La hawla... (Abu Dawud 832, Hasan); Hanafi accepts a translation, Maliki and Hanbali do not.
Calls mushaf reading in prayer makruh tahriman for Hanafis (al-Hidayah: Abu Hanifa held it invalidates); 'what invalidates prayer' list has no sourceIds; sahw: take the lower count.
Behind the imam: catching ruku catches the rak'ah (Abu Dawud 893); Jumu'ah catch differs (Hanafi: before final salam; Shafi'i: a rak'ah, Nasa'i 1425); khutbah two rak'ahs differ.
Prayer table (Isha to mid-night, later Hanafi Asr, Canadian summer rules); pre-Islam prayers not owed (Muslim 121); seated prayer (Bukhari 1117); Assim al-Hakeem chair video.
preCheckFlags: Recitation card headings 'Ruku phrase', 'Sujud phrase', 'Tashahhud' and 'Salam' lead with Arabic; the naming rule wants plain English first, e.g. 'Bowing (ruku) phrase'.

tool:wudu-ghusl.title: Washing before prayer (wudu and ghusl)
keyPoints: Wudu breakers: toilet, wind, deep sleep, unconsciousness; a doubt does not break wudu (Bukhari 137); bleeding, vomit, touching private parts and laughing: Hanafi vs Ireland booklet.
Convert ghusl: Shahada valid without it; recommended in the Hanafi and Shafi'i view but required if in janabah; Maliki and Hanbali reported as requiring it (Abu Dawud 355).
Q&A rulings: wiping socks (Hanafi 3.5-mile test), nail polish, casts (Hanafi vs Shafi'i), wiping a headscarf (Hanbali view), grooming within 40 nights (Muslim 258).
Friday wash: Bukhari 879 calls it compulsory for adult males, the tool treats it as Sunnah (Abu Dawud 354); braids need not be undone (Muslim 330a); tayammum one or two strikes.
Istinja: water after paper (Bukhari 150), left hand (Muslim 262a), paper alone unless spread (Hanafi only); excused-person rule for IBS, leaks or a stoma is Hanafi only (Bukhari 228).
Waswas/OCD: Muslim 132a, Abu Dawud 5112 and Bukhari 5269 for intrusive thoughts; 'OCD affects about 1 in 40 adults' (CAMH, not in the source note); ERP per Najwa Awad.

page:ramadan-planning.title: Ramadan guide: planning checklists and care sections
keyPoints: Cites Quran 2:184-185 as the broad rule for making up days missed through sickness and travel; qada, fidyah, pregnancy, nursing and chronic illness go to a scholar.
Lists menstruation, illness, travel, pregnancy, nursing, medication, disability and serious hardship as affecting fasting; bring in a clinician when health is at risk.
First fast: intention in the heart, break at Maghrib without delay; Taraweeh described as an extra night prayer, usually after Isha.
Laylat al-Qadr plan: one dua repeated, two rak'ahs, a little Quran and charity; says 'Do not treat this app as a calculator or as a ruling for you'.
preCheckFlags: No sourceIds or reviewStatus in this JSON although it cites Quran 2:184-185; only the Ramadan page's hard-coded source list (quran-fasting-2-183-185) covers it.

dawah:personal.title: Dawah Guide
keyPoints: Angels node says angels were created from light and some record deeds, citing only the Hadith of Jibril (Muslim 8a), which says neither; 'created from light' is Muslim 2996.
Quran 5:32 excerpt ('Whoever takes a life... as if they killed all of humanity') drops 'unless for murder or corruption in the land'; check it is quoted fairly.
Crisis referral: 'Emergency services (9-1-1) or crisis support such as 9-8-8'; order is right but '(call or text)' is missing, and scenarios naming self-harm give no numbers.
Jesus content: miraculous birth to the Virgin Mary and miracles by God's permission, cited only to Quran 3:45; 'Allah' is the same God Abraham, Moses and Jesus worshipped.
Arguments for God and oneness: signs of creation (52:35) and 'many gods would pull creation apart' (21:22 excerpt) in the GORAP flow; check they are presented soundly.
'A real smile is a form of charity' (Tirmidhi 1956) has no reference; rights questions go only to the Ontario Human Rights Commission; Quran excerpts use The Clear Quran.
preCheckFlags: No sourceIds: its verses and hadith point to the guide's own 'references' list (27 entries) instead of sources.json entries, as CLAUDE.md requires.
Labels lead with Arabic: the guide title 'Dawah Guide' (eyebrow and breadcrumb) and the suggestion 'Istiqamah'; the naming rule wants plain English first.
